title: Claim Recovery for Distributors
summary: For distributors and stockists: track every claim raised on each principal, tie it to the credit notes received and the principal's ledger, and chase what is still owed.

seo.title: Claim Recovery for Distributors | VipraTech
seo.description: Track scheme, return, rate difference and damage claims raised on each principal, match them to credit notes and ledgers, and recover what is still owed.

designed_for: Owner or CFO of a distribution business
Accounts Head at a distributor or super stockist

problem.intro: A distributor carrying ten or twenty principals raises claims on each of them every month: schemes, returns, rate differences, damages, display and expenses. Each principal settles in its own format and time, partly, late or not at all. The money owed sits across email threads, portals and spreadsheets, and it is often a large share of the distributor's margin.

pain_points.title: No single list of what is owed
pain_points.detail: Claims raised, settled and pending sit in different files for each principal, so nobody knows the total owed at any time.

pain_points.title: Credit notes that do not say what they settle
pain_points.detail: Principals issue lump-sum credit notes that cover several claims, short-pay some lines and give no breakdown.

pain_points.title: Claims that expire
pain_points.detail: Principals set claim submission windows. Claims raised late or not followed up are lost for good.

pain_points.title: Ledgers that never agree
pain_points.detail: The principal's ledger and the distributor's books differ by claims, credit notes and debit notes that nobody has matched.

solution.overview: VipraTech gives a distributor one claims register across every principal. It reads the claims you raise, the credit notes and statements principals send back, and the principal's ledger, then matches each credit note to the claims it settles, including lump-sum and part settlements. Each claim shows its status: settled, short-settled, rejected, pending or close to its deadline. Rejected and short-settled claims come with the principal's reason and a resubmission pack where the claim still holds.
capabilities: One claims register across every principal, with status and age
Matches lump-sum and partial credit notes to the claims they settle
Tracks submission windows and flags claims close to expiry
Reconciles your ledger with each principal's statement
Prepares resubmission packs for short-settled and rejected claims
Shows money owed by principal, claim type and age

workflow.title: Load claims
workflow.detail: Claims raised on each principal are loaded from your sheets, DMS or principal portals.

workflow.title: Load settlements
workflow.detail: Credit notes, settlement statements and principal ledgers are read as they arrive.

workflow.title: Match
workflow.detail: Each credit note is matched to the claims it settles, line by line where the statement allows.

workflow.title: Track status
workflow.detail: Each claim is marked settled, short-settled, rejected or pending, with age and deadline.

workflow.title: Reconcile ledgers
workflow.detail: Your books and each principal's ledger are compared and differences listed.

workflow.title: Recover
workflow.detail: Your team follows up with resubmission packs and a pending list per principal.

match_rules.logic: Each claim is checked against the principal's submission window for that claim type, and claims close to expiry are flagged first.
Credit notes are matched to claims by reference, amount and period. Lump sums are split using the principal's statement or your rule.
Any line settled below the claim needs a reason from the principal's statement. Without one it stays open.
Your books and the principal's ledger must agree once open claims and timing items are listed.
A credit note cannot be counted against two claims, and a claim cannot be closed twice.

exception_codes.meaning: The claim has no credit note past the principal's usual time.
The credit note is below the claim with no reason given.
exception_codes.action: Ask for the breakdown, then resubmit.
Check the reason; resubmit with proof if it holds.

exception_codes.meaning: The claim is close to its submission deadline and still incomplete.
The principal's ledger and your books differ.
exception_codes.action: Send the difference list to the principal.

inputs: Claims raised on each principal, with supporting documents
Credit notes and settlement statements from principals
Your own ledger for each principal
Claim submission rules and windows per principal
outputs: One claims register with status, age and deadline
Credit notes matched to claims, including part settlements
Money owed by principal and age
human_in_the_loop: Your claims team decides what to resubmit, accept or escalate. The system prepares the evidence but never contacts a principal on your behalf.
integrations: Tally, Busy or Marg for your books
Email for credit notes and statements
guardrails: No claim closed without a matched credit note
Lump-sum splits shown with the rule used
Deadlines from each principal's rules, kept up to date by your team
compliance_notes: Credit notes received from principals affect input tax credit; the register shows which credit notes carry GST.

rollout.scope: Your five largest principals, using the last two quarters of claims, credit notes and ledgers.

what_we_measure.how: Share of claims matched to a credit note or marked open with a reason.
Open, short-settled and unexplained amounts across principals.
Claims completed and submitted before their deadline.

faqs.q: We use Tally. Does that work?
faqs.a: Yes. The system reads Tally exports for your books, and claim sheets and credit notes in whatever format principals send.

faqs.q: Each principal sends a different statement format. Is that a problem?
faqs.a: No. Each format is set up once, and new formats are added as they appear.

faqs.q: Can it raise claims for us?
faqs.a: It prepares the claim sheet and proofs in each principal's format. Your team submits them.

faqs.q: Is this for distributors or for brands?
faqs.a: This workflow is for distributors and stockists. Brands use distributor claims settlement to check the same claims from their side.
